verses.pali: อิทัมปิ สังเฆ ระตะนัง ปะณีตัง
verses.english: This too is an excellent jewel in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: เอเตนะ สัจเจนะ สุวัตถิ โหตุ.
verses.english: By this truth, may there be well-being.

verses.pali: ยะถินทะขีโล ปะฐะวิง สิโต สิยา
verses.english: Just as a locking post, planted firm in the earth,

verses.pali: จะตุพภิ วาเตภิ อะสัมปะกัมปิโย
verses.english: cannot be shaken by the winds from the four quarters,

verses.pali: ตะถูปะมัง สัปปุริสัง วะทามิ
verses.english: so, I say, is the true person to be likened —

verses.pali: โย อะริยะสัจจานิ อะเวจจะ ปัสสะติ
verses.english: the one who sees the noble truths with penetration.

verses.pali: อิทัมปิ สังเฆ ระตะนัง ปะณีตัง
verses.english: This too is an excellent jewel in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: เอเตนะ สัจเจนะ สุวัตถิ โหตุ.
verses.english: By this truth, may there be well-being.

verses.pali: เย อะริยะสัจจานิ วิภาวะยันติ
verses.english: Those who make plain the noble truths,

verses.pali: คัมภีระปัญเญนะ สุเทสิตานิ
verses.english: well taught by him of deep wisdom —

verses.pali: กิญจาปิ เต โหนติ ภุสัปปะมัตตา
verses.english: however greatly negligent they may become,

verses.pali: นะ เต ภะวัง อัฏฐะมะมาทิยันติ
verses.english: they do not take up an eighth existence.

verses.pali: อิทัมปิ สังเฆ ระตะนัง ปะณีตัง
verses.english: This too is an excellent jewel in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: เอเตนะ สัจเจนะ สุวัตถิ โหตุ.
verses.english: By this truth, may there be well-being.

verses.pali: สะหาวัสสะ ทัสสะนะสัมปะทายะ
verses.english: Together with his attainment of vision,

verses.pali: ต์ยัสสุ ธัมมา ชะหิตา ภะวันติ
verses.english: three things come to be abandoned in him:

verses.pali: สักกายะทิฏฐิ วิจิกิจฉิตัญจะ
verses.english: identity view, and doubt,

verses.pali: สีลัพพะตัง วาปิ ยะทัตถิ กิญจิ
verses.english: and clinging to rule and observance, whatever of it there is.

verses.pali: จะตูหะปาเยหิ จะ วิปปะมุตโต
verses.english: He is wholly freed from the four lower realms,

verses.pali: ฉะ จาภิฐานานิ อะภัพโพ กาตุง
verses.english: and incapable of committing the six great wrongs.

verses.pali: อิทัมปิ สังเฆ ระตะนัง ปะณีตัง
verses.english: This too is an excellent jewel in the Saṅgha.

verses.pali: เอเตนะ สัจเจนะ สุวัตถิ โหตุ.
verses.english: By this truth, may there be well-being.

verses.pali: กิญจาปิ โส กัมมัง กะโรติ ปาปะกัง
verses.english: Though he may still do some evil deed

verses.pali: กาเยนะ วาจายุทะ เจตะสา วา
verses.english: by body, or by speech, or by mind,

verses.pali: อะภัพโพ โส ตัสสะ ปะฏิจฉะทายะ
verses.english: he is incapable of concealing it —

verses.pali: อะภัพพะตา ทิฏฐะปะทัสสะ วุตตา
verses.english: for that incapacity is declared of one who has seen the state.

vocabulary.meaning: the locking post set in a city gateway, sunk deep and immovable. The simile for one who has seen the truths

vocabulary.pali: อะเวจจะ ปัสสะติ
vocabulary.meaning: sees with penetration; sees having gone into it, not merely believing

vocabulary.pali: อัฏฐะมะ ภะวะ
vocabulary.meaning: an eighth existence. A stream-enterer has at most seven more lives, and this is the exact claim made for them

vocabulary.pali: สักกายะทิฏฐิ / วิจิกิจฉา / สีลัพพะตะปะรามาสะ
vocabulary.meaning: identity view, doubt, and clinging to rule and observance — the three fetters dropped at stream-entry, which verses 49 to 51 name one by one

vocabulary.pali: จะตุ อะปายะ
vocabulary.meaning: the four lower realms. Freedom from them is the second thing claimed here

vocabulary.pali: ฉะ อะภิฐานานิ
vocabulary.meaning: the six great wrongs — the deeds one who has seen the state is constitutionally unable to commit
one who has seen the state; the last word of this stanza and its whole ground

checks.issue: ต์ยัสสุ BEGINS WITH A MARKED CONSONANT, which is unusual — the ์ cluster mark sits on the very first letter of the line, so the word opens with the cluster ty-. Romanised tyassu with the mark dropped, the same treatment every other cluster mark in this book gets. Read at 2.6x; the mark is clear and sits over the ต, not over anything before it.

FOUR STANZA OPENINGS, MEASURED. Verses 36, 42, 48 and 56 start at x 960 where every other line starts at x 870-880 — a consistent 80-90px indent, measured line by line across the whole sheet, and nothing else is indented. Same treatment as page 83, which indents its five. NOTE that the first attempt to measure this used page 83's absolute threshold and reported every line as indented; the baseline moved between the two sheets, so the indent has to be measured RELATIVE to the block, not against a fixed x.

SINGLE COLUMN, MEASURED: ink x 860 to x 1660 with no empty band inside it. The block also sits further right than page 83's, which is why a fixed threshold failed — profile the block's own left edge first, then the indents against it.

อัฏฐะมะมาทิยันติ IS THE DOCTRINAL CLAIM OF THIS STANZA and worth reading carefully: na te bhavaṃ aṭṭhamamādiyanti, 'they do not take up an eighth existence' — the standard statement that a stream-enterer has at most seven more lives. Reproduced as printed; the English states it plainly rather than glossing it away.

THE TWO CLOSING LINES REPEAT FOUR TIMES EACH ON THIS SHEET — อิทัมปิ สังเฆ ระตะนัง ปะณีตัง at verses 34, 40, 46 and 54, and เอเตนะ สัจเจนะ สุวัตถิ โหตุ. at 35, 41, 47 and 55 — word for word identical every time. Not duplication: every stanza of this sutta closes the same way. Recorded because check_render walks strings in printed order and eight verbatim repeats on one page is exactly the shape that reads as a fault.

EVERY อิทัมปิ LINE ON THIS SHEET IS FOR THE SAṄGHA, none for the Buddha or the Dhamma, because these stanzas are all in the Saṅgha section. Page 83 had พุทเธ once and ธัมเม twice. Worth stating so the repetition is not mistaken for a copied line.

THE SHEET RUNS OUT MID-STANZA but verse 59 is a whole printed line, so no […] marker is used — it is the stanza that is unfinished. The entry carries BOTH continuation_of AND continues: true, which is what page 83 was caught missing and what check_batch now enforces.
